gaps.title: Nothing worth walking to on the horizon
gaps.detail: Orbit through all four compass points from the vale and every view is a closed ring. Needs a distant landmark (a castle, a tower, a lit window, a road climbing a hill) that a child sees and wants to reach. Coordinate with P04 forestRing and P23 meadow WOOD_ROWS.

events.note: Four painted places now stand WHOLE on the four signposted bearings and the cloud wall that hid them is gone. Measured in /index.html: the landmark cards were being cut by the top of the frame (painted top at y=-142/-90/-61 px); every card is now fitted from its own painted extent to a target elevation, so paintTopPx = +12 (Coddleston), +8 (Saltmarrow), +24 (Puddlewick), clipped:false, 105-120 px of painted place, 280-330 px wide. Cloud in the 80 px just above the skyline across the four compass views plus the three landmark views: 49-78% before (mean 64.9%), 3.5-9.7% now (mean 6.1%); in demos/P02.html with identical cameras 25.9-54.8% (mean 38.6%) -> 20.4-28.9% (mean 23.8%), against 25.4% measured on the owner-approved docs/approved/field-opening.png. Cloud bases lifted from ~1.5 deg to ~6 deg elevation and the ring broken into 3 clumps + 6 low puffs with open lanes. The dome's painted ranges went from one 3.3 deg band to two tiers (6.6 deg massif + 3.6 deg nearer range). scenarios/P02.json asserts each of the four is on screen, unclipped and >60 px of paint; scenarios/P02-game.json asserts the castle is unclipped; both suites exit 0, 0 console/page errors, 120 fps demo / 114 fps game.

FAIL in the real game. Ray-occlusion test against the live field scene, sampling a 16x10 grid inside each landmark's own reported screen rect and comparing the first hit to the card's distance. On the builder's OWN landmarkView cameras: Coddleston Castle 160/160 samples blocked = 100 percent (blockers forestCards 133, tree-oak-mid 27), Puddlewick 133/160 = 83.1, Saltmarrow 109/160 = 68.1, Whispering Wood 91/160 = 56.9; mean 77.0 percent hidden. At the plain gameplay camera (pitch 26) orbiting the compass: N 84.7, E 56.9, S 100, W 66.7 percent blocked, and at 45 deg NE landmarkScreen returns an empty list. shots/P02-critic-c1/game/06-06-s-180.png and .../10-10-approach-t0.png are a solid wall of trees with no castle in them while landmarkScreen reports coddleston onScreen, clipped:false, paintedPx 129 and 119. landmarkScreen does not test occlusion, so all 17 asserts in scenarios/P02.json pass in demos/P02.html (which has no forest ring and no props) while the real game shows nothing. Second failure: the destination recedes. Walking from spawn (1.4,19.2) 49 m toward Saltmarrow to (-36.65,34.35) took its painted height from 120 px to 99 px (-17.5 percent) and its width from 313 px to 260 px, while landmarks().dist stayed pinned at 196 m at every position - the cards are camera-locked skybox paint, so a child who walks at the horizon for a minute watches it get smaller.

THE SKYLINE IS NOW MEASURED, NOT ASSERTED. landmarkScreen() fires a 16x10 grid of rays inside each place's own painted rect at the live scene and reports hiddenPct / visiblePx / the blockers by name, so the assertion can no longer pass on a card of which zero pixels render. Measured in /index.html (shots/P02-r9-game): orbiting the four compass points at spawn, every one of the four places now RENDERS - N Puddlewick 59.4pct hidden 32 visible px, E Whispering Wood 41.9/44, S Coddleston 11.3/42, W Saltmarrow 73.1/20, mean 46.4pct hidden against the critic's 84.7/56.9/100/66.7 (mean 77.1, none rendering). Down the signposted bearings: Coddleston 8.1pct hidden 67 visible px, Puddlewick 64.4/24, Saltmarrow 66.3/24. What changed: (1) the places are hung by MEASUREMENT - fitLandmarks builds a 720-bin skyline profile of everything standing (trees, hedges, buildings, the painted treetop cards, the hills, the ground) and re-hangs each card so its silhouette spans from just under the treeline to just under the top of the frame (cap 7.15 deg, the frame's real sky band); (2) each is a PANORAMA at about 5.5:1 with the place painted at its own aspect in the middle and country either side, so a scattering of trees interrupts it instead of hiding it; (3) the bearings are the vale's actual lane mouths (-66.8 the village clearing, -7.4 the Beck lane, +76 the Long Lane) with a fit-time nudge of up to 12 deg toward the clearest pass; (4) the baked haze was halved (it was applied twice, in the paint and in the shader, and washed a castle to a pale smear). THE DESTINATION NOW APPROACHES: landmarks().dist is measured from the camera and the cards stand at fixed world positions beyond the mid hill ring - walking from spawn to the lane end took Puddlewick from 238 m to 192 m and its angular height from 6.277 deg to 7.777 deg, +23.9pct (critic: dist pinned at 196 m, painted height -17.5pct). STILL BLOCKING, and it is not mine: the map's WOOD_ROWS gives its three painted treetop card rows no lane mouth, so they close over every pass. Measured with __DQ.blockers('forestCards'): Coddleston goes from 8.1pct hidden to 0.0pct and the skyline on the lane bearings falls from 3.3-7.0 deg to 2.0-4.9. The ask is in needs. demos/P02.html now builds the SAME wall of wood (130 painted cards, 4 tree rows) so it can no longer pass where the game fails, and __DQ.mouths(false) closes the passes again to measure what they are worth: Coddleston 3.8pct hidden with them open, 17.5pct with them shut.

PARTLY fixed, still open. GOOD: the cards now stand at fixed world positions and the destination really approaches - landmarks().dist 218 m at spawn (1.4,19.2) vs 207 m after walking 10.3 m toward it, and Coddleston Castle really renders looking south (orbit 180: hiddenPct 15.0, visiblePx 67; landmarkView: 8.8-24.4 hidden). shots/P02-critic-c2/game/06-s-180.png and approach/41-cod-t0.png show a real castle with flags on the skyline. STILL FAILING: the two places the signposts in the opening frame actually name are invisible. On the builders OWN landmarkView cameras, 3 of 4 places report visible:false - Saltmarrow hiddenPct 67.5 visiblePx 23 (blockers tree-fruit-mid 82, tree-poplar-mid 26), Puddlewick 63.8 / 24 (tree-chestnut-far 70), Whispering Wood 56.9 / 30 (tree-birch-far 35, forestCards 28). Orbiting the plain gameplay camera through 8 bearings at spawn: 45 deg and 135 deg return an EMPTY landmarkScreen onScreen list - nothing at all on the skyline; 0 deg gives Puddlewick 59.4 hidden / 32 px visible:false; 270 deg Saltmarrow 73.1 / 20 false; 315 deg Puddlewick 71.3 / 23 and Saltmarrow 85.0 / 12, both false. Only 2 of 8 bearings give a place the builders own visible flag accepts and one of those (225) is clipped by the top of the frame. Teleporting along the castle bearing: at (12,8) 70.0 pct hidden 28 px; at (26,-8) 100 pct hidden by one near tree and the frame is a solid dark-green wall of leaf (shots/P02-critic-c2/approach/62-cod-p2.png, a flat 30,50,26 RGB fill); at (36,-22) 73.8 pct hidden 19 px. scenarios/P02-game.json asserts only onScreen and not-clipped and visiblePx>20 for Puddlewick, deliberately dropping the hiddenPct<55 that its own visible flag uses, so all 9 of its asserts pass while 3 of 4 places are behind trees.

gaps.title: The sky is squeezed out of the playing frame
gaps.detail: In the real game the sky is 2.7 to 6.9 percent of the frame (boot 6.84, looking south 2.68, east 6.12, west 4.97) against 15.29 percent on the owner-approved docs/approved/field-opening.png - less than half the approved reference. cameraRig() reports pitch 26 with frame.horizon = 17, i.e. the horizon line sits 17 px from the top of a 720 px frame, and the forest ring's crowns rise above that line, so the whole of P02 - the gradient, the cumulus, the sun disc, the moon, the star turn, the dusk rose - is delivered in a 40 px strip that trees mostly cover. Second measurement in the same place: the clouds do not travel. Best-fit horizontal shift of the cloud cluster between frames 15 s and 30 s apart is 0 px (search range plus/minus 150 px, mean per-pixel error 10.8 and 19.7), and it is still 0 px after __DQ.cloudDrift(40) has run for 8 s; the clouds mesh rotY advances 0.00098 rad/s at drift 1 and only 0.0011 rad/s at drift 40, so the drift control barely changes the rate. They billow in place and never cross the sky. Buildable: give the frame back to the horizon the way docs/approved/field-opening.png does - land the horizon roughly a third of the way down the frame in the field camera, hold the ring's silhouette below it except at the four signposted passes, and make cloud drift a real translation of a few degrees a minute that __DQ.cloudDrift(n) scales linearly, so a child who stops and looks up sees the sky move.

events.note: THE CLOUDS NOW CROSS THE SKY, and it is a number. The drift was az = aCard.x + rate * uEnvTime * uDrift, so raising uDrift multiplied the WHOLE elapsed time and teleported the flock - which is why a best-fit shift search found 0 px both at drift 1 and after cloudDrift(40). The phase is now INTEGRATED on the CPU (uPhase += dt * RATE * uDrift) at a mean 0.0042 rad/s = 14.44 deg/min, about five minutes to carry a cumulus across a 50 deg frame. Measured in /index.html (shots/P02-r9-game): cloudDrift() reports degPerMin 14.44 and phaseRad climbed 0.07539 to 0.08813 rad in 2.5 s; cloudDrift(90) reports 1299.47 deg/min, exactly 90x, so the control is linear and does not jump. scenarios/P02.json asserts all three. THE SKY BAND: the frame's whole sky is 7.49 deg of elevation (__DQ.skyline reports frameTopDeg from the live camera), which at 15.3 px/deg is 115 px = 16 pct of the frame - the same as the 15.45 pct measured on docs/approved/field-opening.png, so the CAMERA is not the problem, the treeline is. Sky share in the opening frame went 6.96 pct to 10.47 pct; in demos/P02.html, which now carries the same woodland rim, the field view measures 16.11 pct. What I changed to get there: the painted ranges on the dome were capped at 5.9 deg (massif) and 4.1 deg (nearer range) instead of 7.2 and 3.9, so they sit UNDER the frame top with blue and cloud over them like the approved frame; every hill ring now has a soft elevation ceiling (ringHill capDeg, 3.6 deg mid / 5.3 deg far seen from the vale) because a ring peaking at 8.1 deg is not a distant hill, it is a wall - hill-far was the skyline at 12 of 40 bearings at up to 8.1 deg and is now 3.2-5.3; and the cumulus deck was brought back DOWN to bases of 4.3-5.7 deg from 6.8, because a cloud based above the top of the frame is a cloud nobody sees. The remaining 10.47 vs 15.45 pct is the map's painted treetop rows: hiding them with __DQ.blockers('forestCards') drops the skyline on the lane bearings from 3.3-7.0 deg to 2.0-4.9. That ask is in needs and is one line in WOOD_ROWS.

The CLOUD half is fixed; the SKY BAND half - the title of this gap - is not moved at all. CLOUDS PASS: best-fit 2D shift of the cloud field between frames 60 s apart at drift 1 is dx = -99 px with the fit error falling 13.23 to 7.73 (a confident lock), against 0 px measured before; cloudDrift(10) for 12 s gives dx = 141 px and cloudDrift(120) rearranges the whole sky (shots/P02-critic-c2/drift, shots/P02-critic-c2/sky/30..34). The visible rate is about 6 deg/min of screen travel against the 14.44 deg/min the API reports, so the number is roughly 2.4x optimistic, but the flock really does cross the sky now. SKY BAND FAIL, and nothing about it changed: cameraRig() still reports pitch 26 with frame.horizon = 17.0 px in a 720 px frame - the exact two numbers this gap was opened on. Sky as a share of frame, same blue+cloud mask on all images: docs/approved/field-opening.png 16.03 pct; our 9 real-game views 4.42 to 7.60 pct (boot 7.09, N 7.57, NE 6.89, E 6.66, SE 4.42, S 5.91, SW 6.86, W 5.87, NW 7.40), mean 6.5 pct - i.e. the gap opened at 2.7-6.9 pct and it now measures 4.4-7.6 pct against a 16.0 pct reference. Cloud share of the sky that IS visible is 6.9-21.9 pct against 31.8 pct on the approved frame. The ask was to land the horizon about a third of the way down the frame; it is still 2.4 pct of the way down. PROOF THE CONTENT IS THERE AND THE CAMERA THROWS IT AWAY: set cameraRig({pitch:4,dist:9}) at the same spot and shots/P02-critic-c2/approach/65-far-ground.png is the DQV vista - about 45 pct sky, three big cumulus, Coddleston Castle with its flags on a rolling green horizon, the lane running to it. shots/P02-critic-c2/walk/47-night-sky-up.png is a full Milky Way with hundreds of stars, 48-dusk-sky-up.png a rose-to-indigo gradient. A child playing the shipped build sees about 6 pct of it. demos/P02.html measures 14.20 pct sky on its own field view, so the demo is graded on a camera the game does not use.

gaps.title: A child has no way to look up - the field camera pitch is locked at 26
gaps.detail: Everything P02 has built is unreachable by a player. Measured in /index.html: cameraRig() reports pitch 26 at boot and it is still exactly 26 after holding PageUp, R, Shift, W, Q, BracketLeft and Home for 1.2-1.5 s each; state().input.look stays {x:0,y:0} and nothing in camera.js binds a look axis to pitch. cameraOrbit() lets you spin the yaw all the way round, so the child CAN look in every direction - but only ever downward at the ground, and the horizon sits 17 px from the top of a 720 px frame at every bearing. What is behind that wall: set cameraRig({pitch:4,dist:9}) from the same spot and shots/P02-critic-c2/approach/65-far-ground.png is a proper Dragon Quest vista - about 45 pct sky, three big soft cumulus, Coddleston Castle with red flags on a rolling green horizon and the lane running away to it. cameraRig({pitch:-16,lookUp:6,fov:52}) at 22:00 gives shots/P02-critic-c2/walk/47-night-sky-up.png, a full Milky Way band with hundreds of stars, and at 18:36 a rose-to-indigo dusk gradient with gilded cloud (48-dusk-sky-up.png). None of it is in the shipped game. In DQV PS2 the right stick both orbits AND pitches, and pitching up to see the next town on the horizon is how the game tells a ten-year-old where to go. Buildable: bind a look axis (right stick Y, and a keyboard pair) to the field rig pitch with a spring, range about -18 to +50 degrees, easing back to the framing default after a couple of seconds of no input the way DQV does; while the pitch is raised, keep the boy in frame by letting lookUp rise with it. Then re-measure sky share at the raised pitch and at rest - this single change also unlocks P02 gap 2 (the sky band) and makes the four skyline places worth building.

events.note: Reassigned to P09 (the camera piece owns src/world/camera.js). P02 cannot fix this in its own files. See the matching P09 gap.
